A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same calibration-data study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison, including matching results relocated between tables.

before.justification: v1 reports original pruning experiments on DCLM and LLaMA models, including language-modeling and reasoning results, calibration-data comparisons, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results using synthetic calibration data generated from additional source corpora.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same prefix-conditioned self-generation procedure followed by perplexity filtering. Removing the introduction's reference to a detection strategy does not remove a separately specified calibration algorithm; generation settings change under E3.

E1.justification: Both versions use C4, Wikipedia, SlimPajama, and DCLM calibration corpora, Alpaca language modeling, and the same seven reasoning benchmarks. The added synthesis-source comparisons reuse this existing data and task coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated pruning methods and raw-calibration comparators are retained. Figure 1's comparisons are unchanged, and the magnitude-pruning reference lines clarified in Appendix A already appear in v1. The new Shin et al. citation is not an added evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported generation temperature from 0.6 for DCLM and 0.8 for LLaMA to a uniform 0.6. Generation also expands from 5,000 Wikipedia examples to 5,000 examples from each of four sources. Evaluation tasks, shot settings, and pruning configurations remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether retained LLaMA experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Expanded Tables 2 and 5 test sensitivity to the source used for synthetic-data generation, comparing raw and synthetic calibration for all four corpora instead of Wikipedia alone. Existing sparsity, calibration-size, prefix-length, filtering, and training-similarity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 6.4 newly identifies kernel density estimation as the procedure behind Figure 5's distributions, a limited statistical-method disclosure. The figure itself, 20-seed averaging, and existing standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged; no additional runs are established.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and 5 add C4-, SlimPajama-, and DCLM-derived synthetic results for DCLM-7B and LLaMA-2-7B across three pruning methods. For example, DCLM-7B/Wanda with C4-derived synthetic data newly reports a 64.78 average. Matched earlier scores are retained except that LLaMA-2-7B/OWL/C4 HellaSwag changes from 62.86 to 62.87. The relocated LLaMA-2-13B and LLaMA-3-8B results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The reconstruction objective, generation equation, and Min-K%++ definition in Equations 1–3 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the advertised sampling contribution from two strategies, detection and self-generation, to self-generation, matching the documented method. The central claims about calibration-data importance, training-data similarity, and improved pruning performance remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 adds an interpretation of similar outcomes across generation sources as evidence of versatility, including when available data differs from pretraining data. It also relates improvement sizes to source overlap with pretraining. The stated limitations and future-work boundaries remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page code-repository link and updates the documented generation temperature and source-specific sample pools. Existing dataset, model, and evaluation-tool references remain. Repository accessibility cannot be verified from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Shin et al. (2024), acknowledging prior use of self-generated calibration data to mitigate reconstruction overfitting, and clarifies the present study's distinguishing investigations. The Ji et al. publication update and consolidation of duplicate OWL references do not represent additional research coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, and results discussion receive localized rewrites. v2 also updates affiliations and publication headers and adds acknowledgments. The main section sequence and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v1's combined Table 2 becomes an expanded DCLM Table 2 and LLaMA-2-7B appendix Table 5, with paired raw/synthetic rows, improvement columns, highlighting, and pretraining-membership indicators. Older appendix tables are relocated and renumbered. Figures retain their plotted content; Figures 6–8 gain explanations of existing reference lines.

improvement.justification: The added source comparisons strengthen support for the method beyond v1's Wikipedia-only synthesis experiments. Clearer contribution statements, acknowledgment of closely related work, and a code link also improve the paper. These are limited gains; the unexplained LLaMA temperature revision alongside retained scores leaves some reproducibility ambiguity.
